input: Shadow a local city council meeting this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who this is for (a student, a journalist, a curious resident, a professional) determines the level of preparation, note-taking depth, and follow-up actions needed.
Whether they want to attend just one meeting or multiple sessions, and whether they want to shadow a specific committee or a general session, changes the research and planning required.
Which city or municipality they are targeting determines where to look for meeting schedules, how accessible the meetings are, and what local rules apply to public observers.
Knowing what they hope to get out of it — e.g., understanding procedures, researching a specific issue, networking, completing an assignment — shapes what to focus on before, during, and after.
Their availability this month (evenings only, weekdays, specific dates) determines which meetings they can realistically attend, since council meetings are often scheduled at fixed times.
Whether they want to actively engage (public comment, speaking to officials) or strictly observe quietly affects how they should prepare and present themselves.
Knowing whether they have already identified a meeting or need help finding one, and whether they need any preparation materials (agenda, background reading), determines the immediate first step.

gold.taskTitle: Shadow a local city council meeting this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to attend and observe a local city council meeting sometime this month, likely to learn how local government works or for a specific personal, academic, or professional purpose.

questions.title: Who is this shadowing experience for?
questions.description: Is this for yourself as a curious resident, for a school or university assignment, for professional research, or another role? This shapes the depth of preparation and follow-up needed.

questions.title: Which city or council are you targeting?
questions.description: Identifying the specific municipality determines where to find the meeting schedule, agendas, and any public observer rules.

questions.title: Do you want to attend one meeting or several?
questions.description: Attending a single session versus multiple meetings or specific committee hearings changes the planning scope significantly.

questions.title: What do you most want to get out of this?
questions.description: For example: understanding how decisions are made, researching a specific local issue, completing a requirement, or meeting officials — the goal shapes what to prioritize.

questions.title: Which days or times are you available this month?
questions.description: Council meetings are typically fixed (e.g., Tuesday evenings) so knowing your availability is essential for matching you to a realistic session.

questions.title: Do you want to observe only, or also participate?
questions.description: Strictly watching versus joining public comment or speaking with officials after the meeting requires different levels of preparation and a different mindset.

questions.title: Have you already found a meeting to attend?
questions.description: Knowing whether you need help locating a meeting and its agenda, or whether you have already identified one, determines the very next action to take.
